lines.text: In 1974, Chinese farmers digging a well struck something staring back at them beneath the earth.
They had accidentally uncovered an underground army of eight thousand life-sized warriors, buried over two millennia ago.
Astoundingly, no two faces are identical: every soldier has unique ears, cheekbones, and facial hair.
China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, built this secret subterranean empire to conquer death itself.
His central burial mound remains unopened, said to contain vast maps of rivers made of flowing liquid mercury.
He conquered seven kingdoms in life, and an entire spirit world in death. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
